record.context_brief: Equilibrium support on non-polytope convex bodies
record.original_question: For compact convex bodies with lower-dimensional faces, beyond hypercubes and more generally beyond convex polytopes, can one obtain analogous results describing how the geometry of the body forces the support of the Riesz-energy equilibrium measure onto lower-dimensional faces? In particular, can this be done for bodies such as the Reuleaux triangle?

evidence.quote: Question 3.1 (Ryan Matzke). Can we obtain similar results for other convex bodies with lower dimensional faces?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Background and setup. For a parameter $s \in \mathbb{R}$, the (generalized) Riesz $s$-kernel on $\mathbb{R}^d$ is
$$ k_s(x,y) = \begin{cases} \|x-y\|^{-s} & \text{if } s>0, \\ -\log\|x-y\| & \text{if } s=0, \\ -\|x-y\|^{-s} & \text{if } s<0, \end{cases} $$
and the Riesz $s$-energy of a Borel probability measure $\mu$ on a compact set $K\subset\mathbb{R}^d$ is
$$ I_s(\mu) = \iint_{K\times K} k_s(x,y)\, d\mu(x)\, d\mu(y). $$
For $s$ in a range where $I_s$ is bounded below and lower-semicontinuous on probability measures supported in $K$, there exists a (unique, under standard convexity hypotheses) equilibrium measure $\mu_K^s$ minimizing $I_s$ over all Borel probability measures supported in $K$.

It is known that for the unit cube $K=[0,1]^d$ (and, more generally, for various convex polytopes), the support of the Riesz equilibrium measure $\mu_K^s$ is forced, for appropriate ranges of $s$, to lie on lower-dimensional faces of $K$ (e.g., on the boundary, or on faces of strictly smaller dimension than $d$).

Problem. Let $K\subset\mathbb{R}^d$ be a compact convex body that is not a convex polytope but possesses lower-dimensional faces (faces of dimension strictly less than $d-1$ in the boundary). Develop analogues of the polytope-case results that describe how the geometry of $K$ forces the support of the Riesz $s$-equilibrium measure $\mu_K^s$ to be contained in (or to concentrate on) lower-dimensional faces of $K$, and identify the ranges of $s$ for which this dimension reduction occurs. As a concrete test case, carry out this analysis for the planar Reuleaux triangle, i.e., the intersection of three closed disks of radius $r$ whose centers form an equilateral triangle of side length $r$.
artifact.status_search_result: A web search for related work on Riesz equilibrium measures and the support's concentration on lower-dimensional faces of convex bodies (with the Reuleaux triangle as a test case) did not turn up any paper resolving the question. Recent work by Matzke and collaborators addresses related questions (e.g., when the support is a sphere under a radial external field, and Riesz energy on cubes), but no analogue for general non-polytopal convex bodies with lower-dimensional faces (such as the Reuleaux triangle) appears to be available, suggesting the question remains open.

status_evidence.title: Riesz Energy with a Radial External Field: When is the Equilibrium Support a Sphere?
status_evidence.snippet: Develops conditions characterizing when the support of the Riesz equilibrium measure under a radial external field reduces to a sphere.
status_evidence.claim: Recent work treats dimension-reduction of the support of Riesz equilibrium measures, but in radially symmetric settings rather than for non-polytopal convex bodies with faces.

status_evidence.title: Geodesic Riesz Energy on Spheres and Projective Spaces — R. W. Matzke (slides)
status_evidence.snippet: Matzke's recent talks discuss Riesz energy minimization on highly symmetric domains; no analogue for the Reuleaux triangle is presented.
status_evidence.claim: No published resolution of the analogue for non-polytopal convex bodies such as the Reuleaux triangle is found.
